hero.title: Facebook post embed pattern
hero.description: Use FacebookPostEmbed to show a public Facebook post, photo, video or reel exactly as posted, instead of keeping a copy of it. It loads lazily and tells you when the post is gone.

stage.label: A stage backed by a Facebook post
stage.fallback: Stored copy: not shown while the post is available.

plainStage.label: A stage with no post
plainStage.description: Stages without an embedUrl keep showing their own text and media.

standard.title: Standard
items: Source of truth for a story is the original post: link to it, embed it, never keep a paraphrased copy that can go stale. If the post is removed from Facebook, the site stops showing it.
Lazy and light: nothing loads until the block is within about 600px of the viewport, and the Facebook SDK is loaded once per page. Posts use `.fb-post`; `/reel/` and `/videos/` URLs use `.fb-video`.
No-JS safe: the plain "View on Facebook" link (`linkLabel`, localize it) is always in the HTML under the embed.

Two kinds of unavailable, both reported through `onUnavailable` so the parent can drop the whole item (keep the callback stable with `useCallback`): (1) deleted or non-public posts, detected live with Meta's tokenless oEmbed endpoint (`oembed_post` answering HTTP 400, code 100); (2) posts Facebook refuses to embed (licensed music, "content owned by someone else"), which oEmbed reports as fine, detected by the placeholder box's fixed 400x225 size once the embed settles.

Only a definite answer is a verdict. A rate limit (HTTP 403, code 4), a network error or a timeout never hides anything. Verdicts are cached in `localStorage` for 24 hours; reads are in `try/catch` and the pattern works without storage.
Use `oembed_post` only, for reels too. `oembed_video` returns success for any URL, including non-Facebook ones, so it can never detect a missing post.

Optional `knownGone` / `knownUnavailableEmbeds`: a site-owned seed list of URLs already confirmed deleted (e.g. `src/data/fb-unavailable-posts.ts`) that are dropped with no network call. Refresh it by probing small batches; Meta's limit tripped after roughly 90 calls in a few minutes.

The 400x225 size test is a heuristic: a genuine 16:9 landscape video embeds at the same size and would be dropped. Check a sample of dropped stages when adopting it on a content set with landscape video.

On `JourneyTimeline`, `embedUrl` replaces the stage's description and media with the post and is dormant when unset, so existing sites are unaffected. Keep the stored text in the data file as the record.

CSP: registered in `tools/csp-registry.mjs` (`connect.facebook.net` script, `graph.facebook.com` connect, `www.facebook.com` and `web.facebook.com` frame); `JourneyTimeline` composes it, so `gen-csp-headers.mjs` picks it up automatically.
